text: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. For me to write the same things to you is not troublesome and for you it is the safe thing.

Watch out for the ‘dogs’, So who are ‘the dogs’? I think it scarcely credible that it could have been the author’s purpose to refer to the same group of people with these three clauses, though this handy gambit does get us off the hook—Paul is really mad at the Jewish proselytizers and souses this triple warning. That said however, I am obliged to confess that I don’t know who Paul was referring to, though the use of the definite article indicates a specific group that the Philippians would recognize. watch out for the evil workers, Might ‘the evil workers’ refer to people within the Christian community? watch out for the mutilation! ‘the mutilation’ is explained, by contrast, in the next verse—it refers to those who insisted on physical circumcision but without a change of heart.
For it is we who are the circumcision, the ones who worship by God’s Spirit and glory in Christ Jesus, and who put no confidence in flesh
(though I myself actually have basis for such confidence). About Paul If anyone else thinks he has basis for confidence in flesh, I even more:
circumcised the eighth day, of the nation of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews; with respect to the Law, a Pharisee;

with respect to zeal, persecuting the Church; with respect to the righteousness that is in the law, blameless. Since Paul did not choose to be born to Hebrew parents, Benjaminites, nor to be circumcised the eighth day, these were advantages of birth. The rest was his choice.
But such things as were gain to me, these I have considered loss for the sake of the Christ.

Yes indeed, in fact I actually consider everything to be a loss for the sake of the excelling thing, the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord The most important thing in this life is to know Jesus Christ as Lord. —for His sake I have already lost everything (and consider it as trash), so that I may gain Christ
and be found in Him, not having as my righteousness that of the Law but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness of God based on faith;

so that I may know Him and the power of His resurrection, and the sharing in His sufferings, The power of His resurrection is something I would really like to have, but if the price is to share in His sufferings.... becoming like Him in His death, We can’t resurrect if we haven’t died.

and so, somehow, “and so, somehow”—this really doesn’t sound like ‘once saved, always saved’. The writings of the Apostle Paul contain a variety of clear declarations to the effect that God is Sovereign; they equally contain a variety of clear declarations to the effect that we are responsible. In spite of having given up everything for Christ, in spite of being an Apostle, Paul is not resting on his laurels, is not taking anything for granted. that I may arrive into the resurrection from among the dead
—not that I have already obtained it or have already been perfected; but I press on to actually claim that for which Christ Jesus claimed me.

Brothers, I do not consider that I have already claimed it, but this: forgetting the things behind and straining toward those ahead, When Paul (he was still Saul) met Jesus on the road to Damascus he underwent a complete change of direction.

I press on toward the goal for the prize, the upward call from God ‘the upward call from God’, that’s the real prize; and the only reason the Father calls anyone is because of Jesus Christ. because of Christ Jesus.
So then, those of us who are mature should have this mentality, but if on some point you think differently, God will reveal that to you as well.

Only, in what we have already attained, let us walk by the same rule, let us be of the same mind. Less than 2% of the Greek manuscripts omit “let us be of the same mind” (as in NIV, NASB, LB, TEV, etc.).

Brothers, join together in imitating me, and having us as a pattern take note of those who walk in the same way. I take this as a personal challenge—to be a pattern that others can use to distinguish between friends and enemies of the cross.
Because many are walking as enemies of the cross of Christ—of whom I told you often, and now tell you even with tears—

whose end is ruin, whose god is their stomach, and whose glory is in their shame; their mind is only on earthly things. Apparently relativistic, humanistic materialists have been around for quite a while.

But our citizenship is in Heaven, and it is from there that we eagerly await our Deliverer, He will deliver us from this world scene, with emphasis upon the glorification of our bodies. the Lord Jesus Christ;

who will transform the body of our humiliation Although as the Psalmist says, we are “fearfully and wonderfully made” (Ps. 139:14), it is also the case that our physical bodies limit us, and not infrequently that limitation reaches the point of being humiliating. Personally, I’m ready and waiting for my glorified body. so that it will be conformed to the body of His glory, according to the working by which He is indeed able to subject all things to Himself.
